title: Opinion on mixed tocopherols, tocotrienol tocopherol and tocotrienols as sources for vitamin E added as a nutritional substance in food supplements ‐ Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Food Additives, Flavourings, Processing aids and Materials in Contact with food (AFC)
authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives, Flavourings, Processing Aids and Materials in Contact with Food (AFC)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (Question No EFSA Q-2005-146, Q-2005-172, Q-2006-265); adopted on 22 February 2008.
result: Table 1 (from Ong 1993 and Sheppard et al. 1993), mg per 100 g of oil: palm oil α-tocopherol 25.6, γ-tocopherol 31.6, δ-tocopherol 7.0, α-tocotrienol 14.6, β-tocotrienol 3.2, γ-tocotrienol 28.6, δ-tocotrienol 6.9; soybean oil α-, β- and δ-tocotrienol 0.2, 0.1 and 0.03; canola oil α-tocotrienol 0.04; no tocotrienols listed for corn, sunflower or olive oil. Tocotrienols differ from the corresponding tocopherols by an unsaturated isoprenoid side chain with three double bonds. Tocopherols and tocotrienols are bioavailable; tocotrienols have shorter plasma half-lives and probably a different tissue distribution than α-tocopherol.
